explain.say: Under an optical mouse, a red LED or an invisible laser shines across the desk at a low angle. The low light makes even tiny bumps and fibres in the surface cast little shadows.

faq.q: Why does an optical mouse have a red light?
faq.a: The light shines across the surface at a shallow angle, so tiny bumps and fibres show up as a speckled pattern the sensor can track. Red LEDs are cheap and bright; some mice use invisible infrared lasers instead.
asks: What is the light under a mouse for?

faq.q: How many pictures does a mouse take?
faq.a: An optical mouse sensor takes from about 1,500 to over 10,000 pictures a second, each only a few dozen pixels across. Fast pictures mean even quick flicks of the hand are tracked.
asks: Is there a camera in my mouse?

faq.q: How does a mouse know which way it moved?
faq.a: Its chip compares each new picture with the last one and finds the shift that makes the speckle patterns line up best. That shift, left or right and up or down, is the movement.
asks: How does a mouse track movement?

faq.q: What does DPI mean on a mouse?
faq.a: DPI, dots per inch, is how many movement counts the mouse reports for every inch it moves. Higher DPI moves the pointer further for the same hand movement.

faq.q: Why does my mouse not work on glass?
faq.a: Clear glass and shiny surfaces have almost no texture for the camera to see, so there is no pattern to compare between pictures. A mouse mat gives the sensor plenty of detail to track.
asks: Why does my mouse jump on a shiny desk?

facts: Optical mouse sensors capture from about 1,500 to more than 10,000 images per second.
Before optical mice, most mice used a rubber ball that turned two rollers, one for each direction.

quiz.say: Why does an optical mouse struggle on a clean sheet of glass?

options.show: There is no surface pattern to compare
options.say: There is no surface pattern to compare

options.show: Glass is too cold for the sensor
options.say: Glass is too cold for the sensor

quiz.why: The sensor tracks movement by comparing pictures of surface texture, and clear glass has almost none.

wrong.0: The link to the computer is not the problem; the sensor cannot see any detail.
wrong.2: Temperature does not matter; it is the lack of texture.
